2. The material facts as stated in the writ petition are that the petitioner No. 1 is a private limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994. The Company was incorporated with the object, inter alia, to construct commercial and residential buildings and it is also engaged in the real estate business in Bangladesh. The petitioner-company has finalised the infrastructure of a project for developing of the most lucrative and biggest shopping complex in Asia in the name and style Jamuna Future Park' in Dhaka. The said project is proposed to contain a multi-storied shopping mall having 5 lac sq. ft (47000 smelter) space per floor and in total there will be 6 floors. The project will contain a 5 Star Hotel, a hospital under joint venture arrangement with an internationally famous hospital in the world. There will also be 140 escalators, an amusement and theme park for children in the said complex along with a bowling court, billiard room, health club, swimming club and auditorium, 7 cinema halls with multi-screen and it will be a first ever such project in Bangladesh. The petitioner No. 2 is the Chairman and Managing Director of the petitioner No. 1-company and it is a sister concern of Jamuna Group of Companies which owns about 20 industrial units. The petitioner No. 1 company for the purpose of constructing the said unit of modern multi-storied residential-cum-commercial complex purchased 2500 decimals of land in CS khatian Nos. 221, 208, 422, 85, 62, 101, 174, 210, 82 ka, 48-52, 54, 165, 179 and CS plot No. 1280-1295, 1302-1306, 1309, 1414, 1439-1453, 1465 and 1572 under mouza Joarshahara District Dhaka. After purchasing the said land the petitioner-company submitted an application on 28-8-2000 under section 75(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 to the respondent No. 1 for permission to use the land for commercial-cum-residential purposes. Rajuk the respondent No. 1, vide memo No. Rajuk/Na:Pa:/21-15(Aa-52)14 Stha dated 14-11-2000 issued clearance certificate for such use of the said land by the petitioner (Annexure-C). Thereafter, the petitioner in accordance with section 3 of the Building Construction Act, 1952 vide application dated 12-9-01 applied to the respondent No. 2, the Authorised Officer No. 2 of Rajuk, for approval of the proposed plan of the said complex in the prescribed form of Schedule Ito the Building Construction Rules, 1996and the requisite fees of Tk. 2,10,000 was deposited along with the application in the form of pay order (Annexure-D). Even after expiry of 45 days of submission of the application the respondent No.2 did not give his decision thereon. In such situation, the petitioner vide letter dated 24-12-01 addressed to the Minister for Public Works complained that they had submitted a plan for the construction of the said complex to the Authorised Officer No. 2 of Rajuk in the prescribed form on 12-9-01. It was also stated in the application that because of inaction of the respondent they are incurring huge financial loss. The said Minister never responded to the letter dated 24-12-01 nor did he take action upon receipt of the same. It has been stated that the petitioners have genuine reason to apprehend that the impugned order has been issued and the approval of the plan is being withheld by the respondents at the behest of the Minister of the Ministry of Public Works with whom the petitioner No.2 has serious enmity and the reason of such enmity being that the Daily Jugantor published and circulated some news items revealing corruption of some ministers including tile said Minister. The reason for such enmity is that the said newspaper, owned by the petitioner No.2, published and circulated the news in respect of the said Minister involving Kala Faruque, a notorious criminal of the country. Although the petitioner No. 2 has no connection with the news reports published in the daily Jugantor yet the said minister has taken it personally and is actively acting in a manner detrimental to the interest of the petitioner and the said minister has also filed defamation case being CR Case No. 2952/02 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the petitioner No.2. The impugned memo at the instance of the Ministe was issued without issuing any prior notice for showing cause and without giving the petitioner an opportunity of personal hearing and, as such, the respondents have grossly violated the principles of natural justice and also violated the fundamental rights of the petitioner No. 2 guaranteed under Articles 27,31,40 and 42 of the Constitution. It has been alleged that without issuing any notice under sub-section (I) of section 3 B of the said Act, 1952 as amended, no notice could be issued under subsection (3) and; as such, the impugned memo is ex facie illegal, as no notice under sub-section (1) of section 3B was ever issued to the petitioners. Plans of other persons have been approved by the respondents within the stipulated period. 

 3. Thereafter, vide letter dated 30-1-2002 the petitioners requested the Chairman of Rajuk to give their approval to the proposed plan of the said complex. The petitioner in the said letter in clear terms stated that because of delay of Rajuk in approving their plan they are likely to suffer huge financial loss, but the respondent No. 1 never responded to the said letter albeit the Rule 7(1)(Kha) of the Building Construction Rules provides that an application made under section 3 of the said Act, 1952 must be disposed of by the Authorised Officer within 45 days. Although 180 days had expired after the application for approval of the plan was submitted on 12-9-01, the respondent No.2 in a most arbitrary and malafide manner withheld his decision on the application. In such situation the petitioner again vide letter dated 23-3-2002 informed respondent No.2 with copy to the Chairman of Rajuk that they had suffered financial loss due to delay of Rajuk in approving the plan. In the said letter, the petitioners in clear terms informed Rajuk of their intention to start the construction of the complex pending approval of the plan. They did not reply to the said letter too. The petitioners assuming that Rajuk has no objection on such construction of the complex commenced the construction and Rajuk, by giving no reply to the letter dated 23-3-02(G), allowed the petitioner by their conduct to proceed with the construction work although Rajuk gave clearance under section 75(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953. After the said letter was addressed to the Rajuk the petitioner began construction work. The respondent No.2, the Authorised Officer, did. not object to such construction, but vide letter dated 10-4-2004 requested the petitioners to submit mutation certificate and rent receipts. In the said letter also the respondent No. 2 did not object to the construction commenced by the petitioner. The petitioner, at the time of submission of the application for sanctioning the plan, submitted mutation certificate and rent receipts and the petitioner by their letter dated 21-5-2002 stated that they submitted the documents asked for along with the application and they are again submitting the same documents. The petitioner uninterruptedly continued the construction work and "completed the construction of infrastructure." Thereafter, the petitioners, to their utter shock and surprise, received the impugned memo dated 17-11-2002 (Annexure-A) issued by the respondent No.2 under section 3B(3) of the said Act, 1952 informing that approval under section 3 of the Act had not been given to the proposed plan and the construction work of the complex was unlawful and the petitioner was directed to demolish the structure within 7 days from the date of receipt of the memo. No order for demolishing any structure can be issued without any show cause notice as required under section 3B(1)(6) of the said Act, 1952. So, the impugned memo is illegal, without jurisdiction and. without any lawful authority. 

 The petitioner No. 1 vide their letter dated 18-11-02 replied to the impugned letter dated 17-11-02 stating that such letter was surprising in view of the pendency of the formal approval of the plan already submitted and also for other reasons and the petitioner requested by that letter to accord formal approval of the plan. It has been stated that the respondent No.2, the Authorised Officer, vide his memo No. Rajukl Na Aa Aa-2/3C-1184/211/76 Stha dated 6-7-02 requested the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for giving their comments on the title of the land on which the said complex is proposed to be constructed and the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka made an inquiry and vide memo dated 1-12-02 gave detailed report to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. The material portion, of the report is as under: 

 The Deputy Collector, Dhaka (Revenue) vide its memo dated 4-12-02 informed the respondent No.2 that the petitioner No. 1 has valid title over the land in question. The respondent No.2, instead of giving the formal approval to the proposed plan, was deliberately delaying the matter and the prayer for approval having not been rejected within 45 days, the respondent No.2 cannot reject the proposed plan .under the rules. The respondents allowed the petitioner to commence the construction work uninterruptedly for 8 months and the respondent No.2 cannot debar the petitioner to proceed with the construction as per plan submitted for their said complex. Therefore, the sanction shall be deemed to have been accorded under the provision of law and the respondents are stopped from refusing to give formal approval to the plan. The Authorised Officer respondent No. 2 cannot act at the dictation of higher authority. There is no scope to withhold the decision on the application filed by the petitioner, but the respondent No.2 is not giving his decision thereon purely for extraneous interference and the petitioners have not been treated in accordance with law. Under the aforesaid situation, the petitioners through their legal Adviser,  Messrs Huq and Company, served a notice demanding justice upon the respondents requesting them to cancel, rescind and withdraw the impugned letter dated 17-11-2002 and to grant formal approval to the proposed plan but without any result whatsoever, and the petitioner was compelled to come before this Court with this writ petition. 

 4. In the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner it has been stated that Rajuk vide Memo No. Rajuk/Na Aa Aa-1/14-M/2002/273 Stha dated 24-5-03 sought permission from the Civil Aviation Authority 'for no objection' for the Future Park on CS Plot No. 1442 and the Civil Aviation Authority vide memo No. CAAB/A-A/ATS/1501/21/2003/ 459/105 dated 21-6-03 gave clearance to Rajuk stating that the building in question can be raised up to 114 ft. (Annexure X). The petitioner also filed an application for installation of deep tube well in the site and the petitioner obtained permission from WASA on 19-1-02. The petitioner also obtained permission for heavy electricity of 1000 KV power from the Government of Bangladesh. Rajukhas given approval or sanction of plan for other complexes in many parts of Dhaka City including Basundhara City and Karnaphuly Garden City which are in the heart of Dhaka City, but refused to give sanction to the plan of the petitioners and, as such, the action and inaction of the respondent are discriminatory. 

 5. The respondents have filed affidavit-in- opposition. Denying the material allegations, the respondents have contended, inter alia, that the notice was served upon the petitioner on 10-8-2002 requesting the petitioner to submit to the Rajuk approved plan within 3 days upon receipt of the said letter and upon failure to produce such document, necessary action would be taken according to law. A report was published in the daily Janakantha dated 10-8-02 (Annexure-A-1) regarding unauthorised construction of Future Theme Park, a project undertaken by the petitioner No.1. Upon receipt of the said notice dated 10-8-2002, the petitioner No.2 neither produced any document nor gave any explanation as to why he could not submit such documents. The petitioner No.2, being the Managing Director of the petitioner No. 1 company, was served with another notice dated 12-8-2002 (Annexure-1 b) to which the petitioner No.2 gave a reply on 13-8-02 (Annexure 1/c), from which it could not be considered that the petitioner had already started construction without any prior approval of the respondent No. 1 and the same was communicated to the petitioner No. 2 by the respondent No. 2 vide memo No. RajuklNa Aa Aa/2C 85/2002/307/Stha dated 15-8-2002. The petitioner was again requested to stop construction work and dismantle the unauthorised construction which was undertaken by the petitioner No. 1 or else necessary action would be taken for dismantling the said unauthorised construction in accordance with the Building Construction Act, 1952 as amended in 1987; and a final notice was served upon the petitioner No.2 on 17-8-2002. The further case of the respondent is that the petitioner knowingly and willfully violated the law and started the construction without an approved plan making the respondents liable for such action taken against them. 

 6. In the affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioners, it has been stated that when all conditions have been fulfilled Rajuk is under legal obligation to give approval to the plan. The approval has definitely been held up at the dictate of higher authority as apprehended by the petitioner because Rajuk has not stated anything why the plan has not been approved. 

 7. Mr Rafique-ul Huq, the learned Counsel has, placing the writ petition and the papers annexed thereto, firstly submitted that the petitioner in order to construct a multi-storied business-cum-residential complex obtained clearance under section 75(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 and submitted the plan for the complex under section 3 of the Building Construction Act, 1952 and the petitioners having fulfilled the legal requirement in submitting the plan for obtaining the sanction the respondent No. 2 was under statutory obligation to accord sanction and/or to approve the plan of the petitioner for construction of the Multi-storied Complex. He has pointed out that at the time of submission of the application for approval of the plain on 12-9-01 the petitioner submitted all the required documents as regards the title and possession and at the direction of respondents the petitioner submitted some more documents, namely, mutation and rent receipts in order to prove the title and possession in respect of the land on which the complex is to be built and that for further satisfaction of the authority the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka by memo dated 4-12-02 submitted a report to the respondent No.2, the Authorised Officer, Rajuk showing that the petitioner-company had valid title over the land in question which report was submitted by the order of the respondents. He argues that the petitioners having fulfilled the legal requirements and no objection having been raised from any quarter, the Authorised Officer, respondent No.2, was under legal obligation to accord approval to the plan submitted by the petitioner-company. He has further pointed out that the plan of the petitioner was withheld by the Rajuk at the dictation of the Minister of Public Works with whom the petitioner No. 2 has inimical relationship. His further contention is that usually the plan has got to be approved if the legal requirement according to the Building Construction Act and the Rules are fulfilled. For the non-fulfillment of any legal requirement the same could have been rejected within 45 days as provided under Rule 7(1) of the Building Construction Rules 1996; but the respondents in the instant case withheld the plan without assigning any valid reason whatsoever. Mr Huq has further contended that the impugned memo dated 17-11-02 (Annexure-A) is ex facie illegal, inasmuch as no show cause notice was issued upon the petitioners according to the provision of section 3B(1)(b) and he argues that at least 7 days' notice ought to have been served upon the petitioner before issuing the impugned memo directing the petitioners to remove or dismantle. Further argument that has been advanced is that, without complying with the provisions of section 3B(2)(3) and clause (d) (i) (ii) (iii) of sub-section (5), action for removing and dismantling the building cannot be taken. Such drastic measure could have ultimately been taken if the petitioners failed to pay fine as mentioned under sub-section (6) of section 3B of the Building Construction Act, 1952. He has pointed out that the petitioners after submission of the plan persistently pursued the matter, which is evident from annexures E & F, but the Authorised Officer being influenced by the concerned Minister withheld the plan and, as such, action of the Authorised Officer is malafide. Before commencing the construction work of the proposed complex the petitioner informed the respondent No.2, therefore, it cannot be said that the petitioners have violated the Building Construction Act. Besides being informed about the commencement of the construction work, the Civil Aviation Authority has given clearance to raise the building up to 114 sq. ft which was obtained by the Rajuk. Mr Haque has summed up his argument placing the relevant provisions of the Building Construction Act, particularly section 3B, and in fine, he says that since the plan was submitted fulfilling the legal requirement and the construction was started giving notice to the Rajuk and that progress of construction was within the knowledge of the Authorised Officer, the respondent No.2; the Authorised Officer can approve the plan on receiving the fee/fine as contemplated under clause (d)(iii) of sub-section (5) of section 3B of Building Construction Act, 1952. As regards the statutory authority of the Authorised Officer, he has submitted if the legal requirements are fulfilled and the rules are complied with, in that case the Authorised Officer has no other option but to approve the plan. In support of his submission he has placed before us an unreported decision in WP No. 210/67 dated 27-6-67 where, almost on similar question, Mr Morshed, CJ observed in the following terms: 

 8. Mrs Sigma Huda has appeared on behalf of the respondent Rajuk. She has contended that the construction without obtaining sanction according to the provision of section 3 of the Building Construction Act, 1952 is unauthorised. Her further contention is that although the plan was submitted along with the documents of and the application for approval of the plan, but the authority might have taken some time to verify the title and other aspects of the plan according to Building Construction Rules and that is why there has been delay in giving the decision but the petitioners in the meantime have started the construction unauthorisedly. She has specifically pointed out that the petitioner had already started construction and proceeded with that without obtaining approved plan which is not permitted under the Building Construction Act, 1952 as amended. She has referred to Rule 7(5) of the Building Construction Rules, 1996 and submits that the owner of the proposed building should have served prior notice 7 days ahead of such construction. Sub-rule (5) of Rule 7 is to the following effect: 

 10. It appears from the papers annexed to the writ petition and the affidavit-in-opposition that no such show cause notice as contemplated under section 3B(1)(b) of the Building Construction Act was ever served upon the petitioner asking him to explain within 7 days as to why the proposed construction of the building should not be dismantled or removed nor the petitioner had been given any opportunity of being heard, The respondents however, issued a notice dated 12-8-02 Annexure-1(b) by which the respondent asked the petitioner to stop the construction work and further directed to remove the construction within 7 days and further warned the petitioner to the effect that since the construction is unauthorised proper action will be taken for removing the unauthorised construction under section ঢক(২) of the Act. To what extent the construction was raised or made till then that was not ascertained. The petitioner replied to the notice dated 12-8-2002 by their letter dated 13-8-2002 (Annexure-1(C) to the affidavit-in-opposition) where it was stated that the petitioner submitted the plan on 12-9-01 for commercial-cum-residential complex with the papers and also the clearance obtained from the Rajuk and since the approval was withheld at the instance of the Ministry of Works the petitioner was compelled to start the construction work with the information to the Authorised Officer of Rajuk. Admittedly, after submission of the plan, the petitioners have constructed the complex to certain extent till the notice dated 12-8-2002 served by Rajuk upon the petitioners and what action was taken subsequently with regard to the approval of the plan had not been communicated to the petitioner. The plan is still pending before the Authorised Officer. So, how that plans which is yet to be sanctioned could be dealt with under the provision of law. Sub-section (5) of section 3B appears to be relevant which is in the following terms: 

 12. Now we turn our attention to the question as to whether the petitioners fulfilled the legal requirements when they had applied for approval of the plan. Building Construction Act, 1952 was enacted in order to prevent haphazard construction of building and excavation of tank which are likely to interfere with the planning of certain areas in Bangladesh. For that purpose, certain legal requirements are to be fulfilled for having a sanctioned plan. First requirement was fulfilled by the petitioners in that they obtained clearance from the authority under section 75(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 in view of the dimension and location of the project. Clearance was also obtained from the Civil Aviation Authority as to the height of the building. As regards title and possession, the petitioner submitted documents, mutation, rent receipts and other papers along with the application, and then, at the instance of the respondents, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka reported to the authority and from the report it is revealed that the petitioners have title and possession in the land on which the proposed building would be constructed. The petitioner made persistent endeavour to obtain the approved plan and persuaded the authority to approve the plan but the approval was withheld without any valid reason and the Authorised Officer did not pay any heed to various requests and representations. The allegations that the approval has been withheld at the instigation of the higher authority i.e. the Minister of the concerned Ministry, appear to be not unfounded considering the inertia of the respondent No.2. Since the petitioners had fulfilled the legal requirements the respondent No. 2 was under statutory obligation to approve the plan or to give a decision on that. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondent has not been able to explain as to why the plan submitted for approval has been withheld by the respondents for indefinite period. Therefore, it can be presumed that the respondent No.2, the Authorised Officer, was under the influence of some extraneous factor. The Authorised Officer is authorised to sanction or approve the plan and he is not authorised to refuse the sanction if the legal requirements are fulfilled and the Building Construction Rules of 1996 are complied with, because in case of refusal without any valid reason the fundamental rights to enjoy the property will be infringed. There had been no objection as to the non-fulfillment of the legal requirements or non- compliance of the Rules under which the plan was submitted by the petitioners for approval. Admittedly, the plan was submitted on 12-9-01 and the Building Construction Rules i.e. Rule 7, provides that the plan is required to be approved within 45 days from the date of submission of the application in respect of pucca building, and that period may be extended for further 30 days for the reasons stated in that rule. But delay may be caused for various unforeseen reasons and the time limitation as regards approval of the plan cannot always be followed but, in the instant case, no reasons has been assigned by the respondents. No decision has been communicated at right time. No show cause notice as contemplated under section 3B(1)(b) of the Building Construction Act was served upon the petitioner which we have already stated. So, the impugned notice directing the petitioners to dismantle the building is mala fide, illegal and without any lawful authority being violative of the principle of natural justice. 

 13. About sanction or the approval of the plan on payment of 10 times fee/fine of the amount prescribed there is no legal predicament. Ultimate action for removing or dismantling the building already constructed should be taken if the petitioners fail to comply with the provision of clause (d)(i)(iii) of sub-section 5 of section 38 of the Act i.e. when the petitioner fails to pay the fine or fee in obtaining the sanction. In that view, the impugned memo No. Rajuk/Na Aa Aa/2C85/ 2002/599/Stha: dated 17-11-02 (Annexure-A) is declared to have been issued without any lawful authority. Since the petitioner had already prayed for approval of the plan which is pending before RAJUK, the respondents are directed to sanction and/or approve the plan on receiving 10 times fee of the amount prescribed within two months from the date of receipt of the judgment. The respondents may, however, at the time of approval verify the plan in the context of the Building Construction Rules, 1996.
